$comment: THE brand-asset contract. scripts/gen-icons.mjs RENDERS from it and
scripts/check-brand-icons.mjs VERIFIES the committed files against it, so a
safe-area number exists in exactly one place and cannot drift between the
History: the 1024px master used to carry ~11.7% transparent padding per edge.
gen-icons treated that framing as authoritative (appIcon coverage 1, no crop),
so EVERY derivative inherited it and the mark rendered ~23% small on every
surface -- which was then patched twice at the call site with CSS scaling.
Padding now dies at the source (the master is cropped to its ink and
gen-icons re-normalises on every run) and this manifest is what stops it

master.comment: Cropped to its ink bbox and centred on the smallest square that holds it. Coverage is measured on the dominant axis, so 1.0 means literally zero padding; the mark's own 784x799 aspect ratio accounts for the remaining horizontal slack.

safeArea.$comment: Fraction of the target canvas the mark is allowed to span. One entry per class of surface -- never a literal in the generator.

appIcon.why: Launcher tiles, installer icons and favicons. The master IS the finished icon (rounded plate included), so it goes edge to edge.

adaptiveForeground.why: Android adaptive icons: 72dp guaranteed-visible circle inside a 108dp canvas (72/108). The launcher mask crops everything outside it. Shared with PWA 'purpose: maskable', which has the same contract.

notification.why: Android status-bar glyph: Material system-icon live area is 20dp of a 24dp canvas (20/24).

tray.why: Windows system tray. The tray art is already plate-less and trimmed, so it fills its canvas bar a hairline of breathing room.

defaults.comment: Checker allows +/-3% of canvas width, with a floor of 2px/size so a one-pixel antialias fringe cannot fail a 16px icon.
defaults.alphaDropComment: alpha 'drop' means the OS/spec requires an opaque icon. The generator composites those over the SQUARE brand gradient plate, so the pixels outside the artwork's corner radius continue its own gradient instead of becoming a black notch. Ink coverage is not asserted on them (a fully painted canvas has none to measure); the checker asserts size + absence of an alpha channel instead.

targets.why: iOS/Android legacy launcher icon. Must be opaque; the rounded corners are cropped off because the OS applies its own mask.
Android adaptive foreground layer, drawn over adaptive-icon-background.png.
Adaptive background layer: flat brand plate, no mark.
expo-splash-screen mark. app.json sets imageWidth, so the asset itself must be all mark and no padding.
Android status-bar icon: alpha-only silhouette, tinted by the system. Derived from the dedicated notification-mark source, not the colour tile.

In-app BrandMark source (src/components/BrandMark.tsx): sign-in, Messages panel, rail Home tile, You footer. Transparent, full-ink — the plate's own rounded corners do the rounding, mirroring the desktop demli-logo.svg wrapper. 512px covers the largest step (lg 96dp) at 3x density.
electron-builder app + installer icon.
Windows system tray, 32px (100-150% DPI).
Windows system tray, 16px (100% DPI).
Tray icon with the unread dot composited into the top-right corner; the dot deliberately overflows the mark's safe area, so coverage is not asserted.
16px unread tray icon.
Standalone red dot for the Windows taskbar overlay icon. Not brand art.
PWA manifest icon, purpose 'any'.
PWA manifest icon, purpose 'any'.
PWA manifest icon, purpose 'maskable'. Opaque (the spec forbids transparency) with the mark inside the adaptive safe area.
PWA manifest icon, purpose 'maskable'.

iOS home screen. iOS ignores alpha and applies its own rounded mask, so this is the opaque full-bleed tile. Safari 12 does not read the web manifest, so this link is what makes the founder's iPhone 6 install work.
Also the mark in the inline pre-bundle boot skeleton in apps/web/index.html.
Landing page iOS home-screen icon.
Bundled mark for the landing header (imported by Vite, not served from public/). Header display size is 40 CSS px, so 256 covers even a 3x display.

og:image / twitter:image for getdemli.com. Served from public/ so the URL is stable and unhashed (a crawler needs a permanent link), and opaque because several link-preview renderers composite transparent PNGs onto white.

Landing HERO mark. The hero renders the logo at up to ~272 CSS px, so a 2x display needs 544 device px and the 256 file would visibly soften. Rendered rather than CSS-upscaled: the founder has twice called the landing logo too small, and the fix has to be a real asset, not a stretched one.

icons.why: Browser tab; Safari 12 prefers .ico over PNG icon links.

wrappers.why: Imported by the renderer (AuthScreen, BootSplash, GroupRail) as an URL. Kept as .svg so no component import has to change; the payload is a cropped, recompressed PNG. maxBytes guards the 113 KB base64 bloat this file used to carry.

rel=icon type=image/svg+xml. Browsers render SVG favicons in a restricted mode that blocks EXTERNAL references, so the raster has to be inlined as a data URI -- but at tab resolution, not at 256px like the copy this replaced.

generated.why: Tray, unread tray, taskbar badge and window icon embedded as base64. electron-builder only packs out/ + package.json, so a file under build/ would not exist at runtime.
